clue.text: Thin entertainments

parts.note: a film is also a very thin layer, so cinema pictures are entertainments that are literally thin

explanation.surface: A grumble about a weak evening's shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' reads as a criticism of the shows; it is the other sense of the answer, a fine coating or layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema pictures are entertainments, and the word also means fine layers such as a coating of oil.

clue.text: Miss Day delivered from Cupid

parts.note: a young lady released from the power of the god of love, so free of romantic attachment

explanation.surface: A young lady named Day rescued from the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered from Cupid' means no longer under love's spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not in love, unattached and carefree, has escaped the love god's arrows.

clue.text: Roman poet at Balaclava

definitions.meaning: the author of the Pharsalia, an epic on the civil war
the Earl who commanded the cavalry division at the Crimean battle where the Light Brigade charged

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin epic poet of the Pharsalia, and the cavalry commander in the Crimean War battle.

clue.text: Hush-hush camouflaged ray-only the boss's bird knows

parts.note: hush-hush means kept quiet, private

indicators.note: camouflage disguises, so the letters of the fish word are disguised by rearranging

explanation.surface: A ray hidden in secret, something only the boss's girl is told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camouflaged' rearranges RAY into ARY. The answer is both a boss's assistant (once slang 'bird') and an African bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal assistant works for the boss, and the secretary bird is a long-legged African raptor.

clue.text: Flier of the Red Front shot down

definitions.text: Flier of the Red Front shot down

parts.words: Flier of the Red Front shot down
parts.note: a bird with a red breast, killed by the sparrow's arrow in the old nursery rhyme, dressed up as a fighter pilot downed on a Communist front

explanation.surface: A war report of an airman of the Communist forces downed in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Front' suggests a Communist front line; it is the bird's red breast. In the nursery rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?' the sparrow shoots him with bow and arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme bird has a red breast and is shot by the sparrow.

clue.text: A pretty hook-up

parts.note: a hook-up sounds like a connection, but here it is decorative work made by looping thread with a hook

explanation.surface: An attractive pairing or romantic match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hook-up' suggests a link or a date; the answer is needlework done with a single hook.
explanation.definitionFit: This lacy needlework is made with a hooked needle and is decorative.

clue.text: Cats around Sutton or Luton are in collusion

indicators.note: the cats word goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
both are followed by the same word in place names: Sutton Hoo, the Anglo-Saxon ship burial, and Luton Hoo, a Bedfordshire house

explanation.surface: Cats prowl round two English towns in league.
explanation.walkthrough: Sutton Hoo is a famous Anglo-Saxon burial site in Suffolk and Luton Hoo a stately home; the word they share goes inside CATS. 'are in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in league is a secret partnership, as in 'in cahoots'.

clue.text: Lines from the centre of Leningrad I imagine

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: A Soviet city plan seen from its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'leningRAD I Imagine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokes running from a circle's centre to its edge are its radii.

clue.text: Convert as they try to in " Nuts in May."

definitions.text: Convert as they try to in " Nuts in May."

parts.words: Convert as they try to in " Nuts in May."
parts.note: to convert someone, and what each team tries to do to a player in the children's game, pulling them across the line

explanation.surface: A missionary at a children's party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts in May' (Here we go gathering nuts in May) is a children's singing game where two lines pick a player and tug to pull them across.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone to your side, as the teams literally pull a player over the line.

clue.text: When the headless warrior ancestor appears?

definitions.text: When the headless warrior ancestor appears?

indicators.note: without its head, so the first letter of the warrior word is removed

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior

explanation.surface: A ghost story: the beheaded knight's spectre walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes the K of KNIGHT; and the time a headless ghostly ancestor walks is after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts traditionally walk in the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Cuddle a cleric in stock fashion

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
the cloth stands for the clergy, so a cleric is one of the cloth

explanation.surface: Someone embraces a clergyman in a conventional manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like an adjective (stock fashion = usual way); it is the noun, a wide band worn round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock is an old-fashioned wide cravat or band of cloth worn round the throat.

clue.text: Carrying out murder to get a thousand dollars

parts.note: to do in is slang for to murder
G, a grand, is American slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A hired killing done for a fee of a grand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Carrying out' a contract killing; it is just the definition, performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing a task is the act of executing it.

clue.text: Over there a docked horse for Charlotte

parts.note: yon is an old word for that one over there

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter of the horse word is cut off

parts.note: gee, or gee-gee, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Pointing out a horse with a cropped tail, meant for a girl called Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' removes the last E of GEE. Charlotte M. Yonge was a Victorian novelist, author of The Heir of Redclyffe.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Mary Yonge was a prolific Victorian novelist, so her first name stands for her.

clue.text: Hiking in the Ridings?

parts.note: walking, said in slang that mentions hooves, as if the walkers were riding horses

explanation.surface: Walking holidays in rural Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings were the old divisions of Yorkshire; 'Ridings' also suggests riding a horse, whose hooves make the slang phrase for going on foot apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on foot is slang for walking, which is what a hiker does.

clue.text: Having a right royal time

parts.note: 'right royal' is a phrase for a grand time, but read literally it means holding the royal right, that is reigning

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a splendid party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a right royal time' sounds like great fun; read literally it is a period on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A regnant monarch is one who is reigning in their own right, spending their time as sovereign.

clue.text: Proceed to wager — think an intermediary's needed

definitions.note: here 'intermediary's needed' means an intermediary is needed, so the noun stands alone

parts.note: to go is to proceed
a bet is a wager
ween is an archaic verb meaning to think or suppose

explanation.surface: Advice to place a bet and find a middleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ween' is an old word for think, seen in 'overweening'.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman carries messages between two parties.

clue.text: Avuncular statesman gets eggs right for tea

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the US government, so an uncle-like statesman is Sam
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A kindly politician has eggs at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avuncular' means uncle-like, pointing to Uncle Sam. The definition 'for tea' describes the urn by its use.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian urn used for boiling water to make tea.

clue.text: Old princely tomb-spoilers.?

parts.note: split differently, the title reads as people who spoil burial places, while it really names German noble rulers

explanation.surface: Ancient royals who robbed graves.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MAR (spoil) GRAVES (tombs), the title means tomb-spoilers; margraves were German princes ruling border provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a hereditary German prince of a border territory.

clue.text: Sheep having lost his wool's subject to many a blast

definitions.text: Sheep having lost his wool's subject to many a blast

parts.words: Sheep having lost his wool's subject to many a blast
parts.note: a sheared male sheep, plus the 's, gives horns that are blown, as at Jericho

explanation.surface: A shorn sheep left exposed to the cold winds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RAM SHORN + 'S, a sheep that has lost its wool; ram's horns are blown as trumpets (the shofar, the walls of Jericho), so 'blast' is a horn blast, not wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Horns of male sheep are blown as trumpets, as in the shofar.

clue.text: Got taken in by some cove

definitions.text: Got taken in by some cove

parts.words: Got taken in by some cove
parts.note: 'cove' looks like slang for a chap who tricks someone, but it is a small bay that encloses a ship

explanation.surface: A victim of some fellow's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' is old slang for a man, so the surface reads as being swindled; it is a coastal inlet, and a ship caught in a bay is so described.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed within a bay, as a ship is held in by a curving coast.

clue.text: Thirsty work for Dobbin and a quencher

definitions.meaning: Dobbin is a stock name for a farm horse, and pulling loads is a carthorse's work

explanation.definitionFit: Hauling is the work of a carthorse, and a long gulp of drink quenches thirst.

clue.text: He's seen to be right in front of the vehicle

indicators.note: the right letter is placed before the vehicle word in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
a tram is a vehicle running on street rails

explanation.surface: A man stands just ahead of a bus or tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' supplies BE as written. Bertram is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertram is a male first name, so 'he' fits any man so named.

clue.text: - Heaps of earth to wheel

explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric burial mounds, and handcarts pushed on a wheel.

clue.text: Mobile sitz ?

parts.note: a sitz bath is one you sit in; a mobile seat for invalids also joins the words for a bath and a seat

explanation.surface: A portable hip bath.
explanation.walkthrough: A sitz bath is a shallow bath for sitting in (German sitzen, to sit); the answer is a wheeled seat for invalids, once common at spa towns like Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled hooded chair for invalids is moveable seating, the sense of 'Mobile' here.

clue.text: Shipton, Lincs. ?

parts.note: an invented town name made from a ship, pointing to a real Lincolnshire town that sounds like a two-masted vessel

explanation.surface: A village in Lincolnshire named after boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigg is a market town in Lincolnshire; a brig is a two-masted sailing ship, so a 'ship town' in Lincs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lincolnshire market town bears the name of a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Provide for the movement of tanks ahead of the columns

definitions.text: Provide for the movement of tanks ahead of the columns

parts.words: Provide for the movement of tanks ahead of the columns
parts.note: a verb for providing food, which placed before a word for columns gives the tracks that tanks move on

explanation.surface: Arranging supplies as armoured units advance before the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide for' is the definition; the answer ahead of PILLAR (columns) makes CATERPILLAR, the tracks tanks move on.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide food and supplies for people.

clue.text: As far as one can get along the river ?

definitions.text: As far as one can get along the river ?

parts.words: As far as one can get along the river ?
parts.note: the extent one can stretch to, and also a straight stretch of a river

explanation.surface: How far a boat can travel upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both the distance one can stretch to and a straight stretch of river between bends.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent, and a level stretch of water on a river.

clue.text: Yes, an Hon. may unbend in Northants

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect form of yes

indicators.note: unbending loosens the shape, so the letters of the title abbreviation are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat relaxes on a visit to Northamptonshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may unbend' rearranges HON into NHO. Aynho is a village in Northamptonshire (Northants), an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Aynho is a village located in the county of Northamptonshire.

clue.text: I alter the rent without risk of action

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters of the following word are reorganised

explanation.surface: A landlord changes the rent with nothing to fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' rearranges RENT into NERT, which follows I given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inactive is incapable of moving or reacting, so it poses no danger of doing anything.

clue.text: He became a Gilbertian " Square "

parts.note: the aesthetic poet in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience turns into a commonplace young man, and the name is also a London square

explanation.surface: A man turned into a stuffy character from a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: In Patience, Archibald Grosvenor gives up being an idyllic poet to become an ordinary 'matter-of-fact young man'; Grosvenor Square is in Mayfair, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Patience character abandons aestheticism for conventionality, and the surname also names a famous London square.

clue.text: Our Eugene scolds — creates

parts.note: Gene is the familiar short form of the name Eugene
to rate someone is an old word for to scold them

explanation.surface: A family member called Eugene tells people off, then makes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate' in the sense of berate is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce or bring into being is to create.

clue.text: Taxes for kilts ?

definitions.meaning: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
kilts stand for the people of Scotland who wear them

explanation.definitionFit: Old levies, as in going scot-free, and the people of Scotland, known by their kilts.
